summary: Baddeck Harbour's light on Kidston Island, Cape Breton: lit in 1875 as a red light, rebuilt as a wooden tower in 1911, now a long-flashing green, reached only by boat.

access.note: Reached only by boat. Site open, tower closed (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends). A Lions Club ferry runs in July and August (Rowlett).

events.note: New light tower erected on the north-east point of Kidston Island (Department of Marine announcement, quoted by LighthouseFriends).
Put in operation 8 November 1875: fixed red, 31 ft above high water.
Donald McRae appointed keeper at $200 a year, including a boat allowance.
Shelf holding the lamps raised six inches.
Donald McRae appointed 17 May 1892 (1909 list gives the year; 1911 list gives the day and month at Kidston Island).
Fourth-order 270-degree lens replaced the reflector apparatus (LighthouseFriends gives 1909). The Department's report for the year ended 31 March 1910 describes the change as done.
New square wooden tower replaced the original; L. Mury of West Arichat built it (LighthouseFriends). Rowlett gives 1911 for the present tower.
Original tower taken down: Rowlett says not demolished until 1959; LighthouseFriends says finally destroyed in 1959.
Ownership of the lighthouse transferred to the Village of Baddeck.

corrections.why: The standing tower is the 1911 replacement, a square wooden tower. The 1875 tower was a smaller tower that was taken down or destroyed in 1959 (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends).
1959 is the year the original tower was taken down, not a first-lighting date. The light was first lit on 8 November 1875 (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1875 light was a fixed red (LighthouseFriends, quoting the Department). The present light is a long-flashing green, LFl G 12s, with 2 s flash and 10 s eclipse (Canadian Coast Guard; Rowlett gives green 2 s on, 10 s off). The record's Fl G 12s drops the long flash; the Coast Guard list is the authority. The date of the change is not in the sources.
1959 is the year the original tower was taken down (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends), not a first-lighting date. The light dates from 1875.

notes_for_editor: Ownership is disputed. Rowlett and the Coast Guard's 'private aid' entry fit the village ownership from 2005 that Rowlett and LighthouseFriends' own history give. LighthouseFriends' visitor notes say the Coast Guard owns the lighthouse, and the story reports both. The LighthouseFriends paragraph saying the original tower 'was going to be demolished after a replacement tower was built in 1991' contradicts its own 1959 date and is left out. Focal heights differ: LighthouseFriends gives 48 ft (14.6 m) for the 1911 tower; Rowlett gives 13.5 m (44 ft) and the Coast Guard 13.3 m for the present light. Wikipedia gives 1912 for the second tower, 1959 as 'first lit' (a misreading of the 1959 demolition) and 'automated 1960'; these are not cited and the automation date is unsourced. Keepers: Donald McRae's 1892 appointment is confirmed in the Department's lists (1909 row: name, 17 May 1892, $240; 1911 row: 'Kidston Island Donald McRae May 17'). The 1902 to 1907 keeper lists also place a McRae beside Kidston's Island, but that is matched by column position and is not cited. Duncan McRae and the 1875 keeper appear only in LighthouseFriends; the corpus of Department lists starts in 1900. The 1875 announcement and cost figures are second-hand from LighthouseFriends, citing 'Annual Report of the Department of Marine and Fisheries, various years'; the 1875 volume is not in the corpus. The 1911-13 Chief Engineer works table (cached volume labelled 1912, scan p. 50) has a row with 'L. Mury, West Arichat' and 'Victoria Foundry Co. Ottawa' and a $626.50 figure, but the station name is not legible beside the row, so it is not cited. Storms, wrecks and rescues: none found. Chronicling America 'Kidston Island' 1875-1925 returned no hits; the 1910 Marine report notes a schooner sinking near the Baddeck wharf, which is not tied to the light; no storms chapter is written. The west-end light (ca-ns-kidston-island-west-end) is a separate station and is not covered here. The date when the light was automated is not in any source read, and the keeper roster runs to at least 1937 (LighthouseFriends). The lighthouse record's 'status: active' does not show the Coast Guard's 'Seasonal' note; that is in the story. Checked on page images, 2026-10-28: the 1909 row (printed p. 160, scan 167) reads 'Kidstone's Island, Donald McRae, May 17, 1892, $240'. The 1911 row (scan 244, printed page 237) reads 'Kidston Island, Donald McRae, May 17'; its year column reads 1892. The 1910 entry (printed p. 92) reads '4th order 270 dioptric illuminating apparatus has been substituted for the catoptric apparatus heretofore used'. The story's 'best seen' superlative was replaced with the marina and waterfront wording the sources give.
